# NSSFactory r3 — Lalande 21185

_More roads to the same light._

r3 brings a Vulkan plugin as a preview, adds PNLM, takes BM3D's group transform back to the paper's Haar, makes the GPU block matching faster with the same matches, and keeps GPU frames on the GPU under VapourSynth R81 (`nss_cuda`) and R80+ (`nss_vk`).

**Work in progress.** The packages below are preview builds for evaluation, not stable releases. `nss_vk` is a further preview: only NLM, BM3D and PNLM are ported, and it is validated on NVIDIA GPUs only.

## Packages

| Package | Plugin | Runs on |
|---|---|---|
| `nssfactory-r3-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | `libnss.so` (`nss`) | x86-64 with AVX2; glibc 2.34 and the libstdc++ of GCC 13 (Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13, Fedora 39 or later). Highway dynamic: AVX2 + AVX3/Zen4 |
| `nssfactory-r3-linux-arm64.tar.gz` | `libnss.so` (`nss`) | AArch64 with glibc 2.38 (libstdc++ built in). NEON |
| `nssfactory-r3-macos-arm64.tar.gz` | `libnss.dylib` (`nss`) | Apple silicon, macOS 13.3 or newer. NEON |
| `nssfactory-r3-windows-x86_64.zip` | `libnss.dll` (`nss`) | x86-64 with AVX2 and the Visual C++ 2015–2022 Redistributable |
| `nssfactory-r3-linux-x86_64-cuda.tar.gz` | `libnss_cuda.so` (`nss_cuda`) | as `linux-x86_64`, with an NVIDIA driver r580 or newer (CUDA 13) |
| `nssfactory-r3-windows-x86_64-cuda.zip` | `libnss_cuda.dll` (`nss_cuda`) | an NVIDIA driver r580 or newer (CUDA 13) and the Visual C++ Redistributable |
| `nssfactory-r3-linux-x86_64-vk.tar.gz` | `libnss_vk.so` (`nss_vk`) | a Vulkan 1.3 device with the features in the [Vulkan reference](https://github.com/AmusementClub/vapoursynth-nssfactory/blob/master/docs/api/vk/README.md); NVIDIA validated, AMD and Intel untested |
| `nssfactory-r3-windows-x86_64-vk.zip` | `libnss_vk.dll` (`nss_vk`) | a Vulkan 1.3 device with the features in the [Vulkan reference](https://github.com/AmusementClub/vapoursynth-nssfactory/blob/master/docs/api/vk/README.md); NVIDIA validated, AMD and Intel untested |

Clips must be constant-format Gray/YUV/RGB 32-bit float. Each package carries `docs/api`: the [API guide](https://github.com/AmusementClub/vapoursynth-nssfactory/blob/master/docs/api/README.md), the [CUDA reference](https://github.com/AmusementClub/vapoursynth-nssfactory/blob/master/docs/api/cuda/README.md), the new [Vulkan reference](https://github.com/AmusementClub/vapoursynth-nssfactory/blob/master/docs/api/vk/README.md) and the [comparison with other plugins](https://github.com/AmusementClub/vapoursynth-nssfactory/blob/master/docs/api/cuda/compare.md). `core.nss.Version()`, `core.nss_cuda.Version()` and `core.nss_vk.Version()` report `r3`.

## Highlights

- **New: `nss_vk`, a Vulkan plugin (preview)** with NLM, BM3D (spatial and temporal) and PNLM, the same arguments and defaults as `nss` and `nss_cuda`. It takes CPU frames on VapourSynth R78+ and vapoursynth-classic R57.A14+, and keeps GPU frames resident on VapourSynth R80 and R81. On GPU frames at the defaults (1080p YUV420, RTX 5080) it runs BM3D at about 1440 fps, NLM at 820 and PNLM at 990 (`nss_cuda`: 1570, 880 and 780). The other denoisers are not ported yet; `VAggregate` stays CPU-only.
- **New: `nss.PNLM(clip, sigma)`**, patchwise non-local means as Davy and Ehret run it on the GPU (JRTIP 2021): patches on a grid take their most similar patches in a window and in the frames around (`d`), are estimated whole and blended. Over `NLM` at the same window: +0.6 to +2.8 dB spatially (`d=0`), +0.2 to +1.5 dB with `d=1`. Its cost grows much more slowly with the window `a` and the radius `d`: on an RTX 5080 `nss_cuda.PNLM` runs as fast as `NLM` at the defaults and 3 to 13 times faster at `a=8` or `d=2` (1080p gray `a=8, d=1`: 535 against 51 fps). The same bits on AVX2, NEON and CUDA.
- **BM3D model 3: Haar along the group**, as in Dabov et al., instead of the DCT, on every backend. At the paper's settings +0.03 to +0.07 dB, block 16 / group 16 +0.2 dB, the same strength (the best sigma factor does not move); against BM3DCUDA at matched defaults +0.03 to +0.09 dB.
- **VapourSynth R81 GPU frames for every `nss_cuda` filter:** a GPU-resident clip (`std.GPUUpload`, another GPU filter's output) stays in video memory through the filter, so a chain of GPU filters skips the copies to and from host memory. On by default on R81; `NSS_CUDA_GPU_FRAMES=0` turns it off. Other cores download GPU clips first, as before ([GPU frames](https://github.com/AmusementClub/vapoursynth-nssfactory/blob/master/docs/api/cuda/README.md#gpu-frames)).
- **Faster block matching on the GPU, with the same matches.** A candidate-parallel matcher on CUDA and Vulkan stages the search window in shared memory for one-channel searches with blocks 2 to 8, 12 and 16: it takes BM3D's default search (and WNNM's and NCSR's), windows up to `bm_range=64`, groups up to 64 and the centre frame of temporal searches, with the same matches, distances and order as before. BM3D shares the matching work whenever `block_size` is twice `block_step` (Davy and Ehret's square matcher: 1080p 1.04 to 1.9x end to end, 1.4x at the paper's settings, temporal 1.05 to 1.3x), and CUDA shares exact column sums for block-8 searches at `block_step` 1–3 (1.03 to 1.59x, 1.375x at the paper's settings). The pages list the [optimized search shapes](https://github.com/AmusementClub/vapoursynth-nssfactory/blob/master/docs/api/cuda/bm3d.md#optimized-search-shapes).
- **Direct transfers with vapoursynth-classic.** Under [vapoursynth-classic R57.A14](https://github.com/AmusementClub/vapoursynth-classic/releases/tag/R57.A14) or newer, whose frame-memory extension (`VSFrameMemory.h`) is new in that release, `nss_cuda` copies to and from the VapourSynth frames themselves instead of through staging buffers, for every filter: BM3D 1.5 to 1.7x, WNNM 1.6x, NCSR 1.6x and MCWNNM 1.5x with 3 streams (1080p). Temporal `rolling` modes overlap their chunk copies with the kernels: BM3D and WNNM `radius=1` 1.3x, NCSR 1.4x, MCWNNM 1.45x. Upstream VapourSynth keeps the staged path ([Direct transfers with vapoursynth-classic](https://github.com/AmusementClub/vapoursynth-nssfactory/blob/master/docs/api/cuda/README.md)).
- **NLM weights `wmode` 1–3** (Bisquare A, B, C, as KNLMeansCL and nlm-ispc) on the CPU and CUDA; Welsch (`wmode=0`) is unchanged.
- **Faster CUDA NLM and LSSC with the same output:** the CUDA 13 build (about 1.35x at NLM's defaults over r2's CUDA 12.9 build), register-blocked box sums, `d=1` weight maps shared between streams, two blocks per SM for the larger tile kernels; LSSC builds a frame's dictionaries at once and codes alpha 2.5x faster.
- **The CUDA plugin's host threads sleep while they wait for the GPU:** 1.7 to 48 times less CPU time per frame (NLM 2.8x, BM3D 1.7–6.9x, LSSC 10x, DA3D 48x) at the same speed.
- **What each filter costs.** Each plugin's guide now has a table of every filter's speed at its defaults and at heavier settings closer to the papers: [CPU](https://github.com/AmusementClub/vapoursynth-nssfactory/blob/master/docs/api/README.md#choosing-a-filter), [CUDA](https://github.com/AmusementClub/vapoursynth-nssfactory/blob/master/docs/api/cuda/README.md#speed) and [Vulkan](https://github.com/AmusementClub/vapoursynth-nssfactory/blob/master/docs/api/vk/README.md#speed).

## Fixes

- `memory_limit_mb` is kept at render time on the CUDA plugin, not only when the filter is created.
- `nss_cuda.BM4D` no longer waits forever when frames are asked for out of order.
- A frame that fails on the GPU no longer frees memory that copies still in flight use; out-of-memory during a frame keeps what it holds until the copies are done.
- `nss_cuda` makes no asynchronous copies from pageable host memory, and finishes its creation-time uploads before the streams read them.

## Upgrading from r2

- **Model versions changed:** BM3D 2 → 3 (Haar along the group). Its output changes; legacy temporal intermediates carry the version and must be recomputed (`VAggregate` rejects mixed versions). The other filters keep their models.
- **CUDA driver:** the CUDA packages need an NVIDIA driver r580 or newer (CUDA 13.3); r2's needed CUDA 12.9.
- **`nss_cuda` on VapourSynth R81** keeps GPU clips on the GPU and returns GPU frames for them (r2 had the core download them); CPU clips are unchanged. `NSS_CUDA_GPU_FRAMES=0` restores r2's behaviour.
- **GPU `rolling_chunk`:** `nss_cuda` and `nss_vk` now compute temporal `rolling` output one frame a chunk by default (was 4; the CPU plugin keeps 4). Every frame of a chunk holds a VapourSynth thread until the chunk is done, so larger chunks left the GPU waiting for input at usual thread counts. The output is the same at every chunk size.
- **`nss_cuda` `num_streams`:** the default is now measured per filter; pass `num_streams` to keep a fixed count.

## Known limits

- `nss_vk` is a preview: only NLM, BM3D and PNLM are ported, and it is validated on NVIDIA GPUs only; AMD and Intel GPUs are untested.
- `nss_cuda` GPU frames and the direct transfers with vapoursynth-classic are validated on Linux (RTX 5080); on Windows they are build-tested only.
- PNLM, BM4D and DA3D take the noise's true sigma and assume white Gaussian noise.
- Speeds are measured on one RTX 5080 with a Ryzen 9 5950X; other GPUs are untested for speed.
- NLH's blind estimate still reads textured luma high at very low noise (sigma 5 or less); give `sigma` there when it is known.
